claims.source: More generally, harnessing our understanding of brown-to-white adipocyte conversion may lead to strategies to prevent or delay its course and thus enhance the thermogenic capacity of adipose tissues to mitigate the consequences of metabolic disorders, such as obesity and diabetes.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the potential therapeutic applications of the findings.

results.result: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of mPRAT and iBAT from 1-, 2-, and 6-month-old mice identified four adipocyte subpopulations in mPRAT (mPRAT-ad1-4) with distinct gene expression profiles. mPRAT-ad1 resembles classical brown adipocytes (Ucp1+/Cidea+), mPRAT-ad2 is Ucp1-/Cidea+ and expresses Cyp2e1/Slit3, while mPRAT-ad3 and mPRAT-ad4 resemble white adipocytes with increasing maturity. mPRAT-ad2 represents a unique subpopulation absent in iBAT.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C56 are well-supported by snRNA-seq data (11,708 nuclei for mPRAT, 31,079 for iBAT) with appropriate quality control. The identification of four adipocyte subpopulations is supported by clustering analysis and gene expression data shown in Figures 1G-I. The characterization of each subpopulation is based on differential gene expression patterns. Module score analysis (C53-C56) demonstrates that mPRAT-ad2 lacks correspondence with iBAT subpopulations, supporting its uniqueness.

results.result: Trajectory analysis reveals a progressive brown-to-white transition in mPRAT during postnatal development. The proportions of mPRAT-ad1 and ad2 decrease from 1 to 6 months (43.0% to 33.1% and 36.1% to 23.9%, respectively) while ad3 and ad4 increase (14.7% to 29.9% and 6.2% to 13.1%). Monocle 3 analysis shows a continuous trajectory with decreasing brown adipocyte markers (Ucp1, Cidea) and increasing white adipocyte markers (Npr3, Aldh1a1, Lep) along pseudo-time. This trajectory is absent in iBAT.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C69 are supported by longitudinal snRNA-seq data and trajectory analysis. The compositional changes (C57-C58) are quantified and shown in Figure 1G. Monocle 3 trajectory analysis (C60-C65) demonstrates a single continuous trajectory linking the four subpopulations with appropriate gene expression patterns. The comparison with iBAT (C66-C68) shows a much shorter pseudo-time length (12.8 vs 26.7), supporting the inference of a more stable iBAT population. The conclusion of brown-to-white transition (C69) is a reasonable inference from the combined data.

results.result: Genetic lineage tracing using Ucp1Cre;Ai14 mice demonstrates brown-to-white conversion in the periureter region (puPRAT) but not perivascular region (pvPRAT) of mPRAT. At 2 months, 61.8% of tdTomato+ cells in puPRAT lost UCP1 expression compared to only 7.5% in pvPRAT. These whitened adipocytes display unilocular morphology and express white adipocyte markers (CYP2E1: 34%, ALDH1A1: 23%). Lipid droplet size increased 5.5-fold in puPRAT versus 2.3-fold in pvPRAT from 1 to 6 months. No brown-to-white conversion was observed in iBAT.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-C128 are well-supported by lineage tracing experiments using Ucp1Cre;Ai14 mice with quantitative immunofluorescence data (Figures 3A-I). The regional differences between puPRAT and pvPRAT are statistically significant (p<0.0001). Morphological analysis confirms unilocular lipid droplets in whitened adipocytes. The immunostaining for CYP2E1 and ALDH1A1 (C124-C125) provides evidence that whitened cells can progress to mPRAT-ad3/ad4 subtypes. The absence of conversion in iBAT (C120) is supported by data and consistent with prior literature (Huang et al., 2022).

results.result: Cold exposure (4 weeks at 18°C then 10°C) increases UCP1 expression in mPRAT and iBAT but not lPRAT, reduces lipid droplet size, and counteracts brown-to-white conversion. In Ucp1CreERT2;Ai14 mice, cold exposure significantly reduces tdTomato+/UCP1- adipocytes in both puPRAT and pvPRAT while increasing tdTomato-/UCP1+ (cold-recruited) adipocytes. Lineage tracing with PdgfraCreERT2;Ai14 mice shows that in puPRAT, the 10-fold increase in cold-recruited brown adipocytes is mainly from conversion of UCP1- adipocytes (2.3-fold from ASPC differentiation), while in pvPRAT both processes contribute equally (4.4-fold vs 2.2-fold).
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C144 are supported by multiple complementary experiments including qPCR, western blot, histology, and dual lineage tracing approaches (Figures 4A-K). The cold exposure protocol is clearly defined. The quantification of whitened and recruited adipocytes is statistically significant (p<0.01-0.0001). The use of both Ucp1CreERT2;Ai14 and PdgfraCreERT2;Ai14 mice allows discrimination between ASPC-derived and conversion-derived brown adipocytes. The 100% tdTomato+ labeling in PdgfraCre;Ai14 mice (C141-C142) validates that all adipocytes derive from Pdgfra+ cells. The regional differences between puPRAT and pvPRAT are well-quantified.

results.result: Cold exposure in adult (6-month-old) mice reduces brown-to-white conversion and dramatically alters mPRAT adipocyte composition. snRNA-seq analysis (7,387 nuclei) shows that cold exposure doubles mPRAT-ad1 proportion, eliminates mPRAT-ad2 cells, reduces mPRAT-ad3 by 30%, while mPRAT-ad4 remains unchanged. No enhanced cell death was observed, suggesting mPRAT-ad2 and part of mPRAT-ad3 convert to thermogenic mPRAT-ad1. ASPC subpopulation proportions remain unchanged after cold exposure.
results.evaluation: Claims C145-C159 are supported by lineage tracing in adult mice (Figure 5A-C) and snRNA-seq analysis after acute cold exposure (4°C for 3 days) in 6-month-old mice. The dramatic compositional changes (C151-C154) are clearly shown in Figure 5E. The absence of enhanced cell death (C155) is demonstrated by Tunel staining (Figure 5—supplement 1G), supporting the inference that cells convert rather than die and are replaced (C156-C157). The unchanged ASPC proportions (C158-C159) suggest limited contribution of de novo adipogenesis, consistent with the lineage tracing results. However, the acute cold exposure protocol (3 days at 4°C) differs from the chronic protocol used in earlier experiments (4 weeks), which should be noted.

results.result: The mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation (Ucp1-/Cidea+) represents a unique cold-recruitable adipocyte type distinct from subcutaneous beige adipocytes. This subpopulation arises from brown-to-white conversion during postnatal life and can restore Ucp1 expression upon cold exposure. While mPRAT-ad2 shares functional capacity with iWAT beige adipocytes to upregulate Ucp1 in response to cold, it has a distinct transcriptome with no overlap with any iWAT adipocyte subpopulation. After cold exposure, mPRAT brown adipocytes are transcriptionally more similar to iBAT than iWAT and likely comprise three origins: recruited mPRAT-ad2, pre-existing mPRAT-ad1, and de novo adipogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C2-C4, C56, C176-C179, C205-C211 are supported by comprehensive transcriptomic comparisons between mPRAT, iBAT, and iWAT under both room temperature and cold exposure conditions (Figures 6A-E). Module score analysis and label transfer methods demonstrate lack of overlap between mPRAT-ad2 and iWAT subpopulations at room temperature (C174-C176, C206). After cold exposure, hierarchical clustering shows mPRAT brown adipocytes cluster with iBAT rather than iWAT (C180, C210). The convergent functional phenotype despite distinct transcriptomes (C205-C209) is explained by different developmental origins (brown-to-white conversion vs ASPC differentiation), which is a reasonable inference supported by lineage tracing data. The three-origin model (C211) integrates multiple lines of evidence.

results.result: snRNA-seq analysis of lateral PRAT (lPRAT) from 2- and 6-month-old mice (6,048 nuclei) reveals a cellular composition significantly different from epididymal WAT (eWAT). lPRAT contains four adipocyte subpopulations (lPRAT-ad1-4) enriched in white adipocyte markers but lacking brown adipocyte markers. lPRAT-ad3 and ad4 show no overlap with eWAT subpopulations, suggesting unique cell types. The ASPC and macrophage populations also differ substantially from eWAT. From 2 to 6 months, adipocyte proportion decreases (70.6% to 46.5%) while macrophages increase (5.7% to 23.8%), with lPRAT-mac1 (expressing Trem2/Atp6v0d2) increasing tenfold.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C109 are supported by snRNA-seq analysis of lPRAT with appropriate quality control and comparison to published eWAT data (Sárvári et al., 2021). The identification of four adipocyte subpopulations (C86-C92) is based on clustering and gene expression analysis (Figure 2D-E). The comparison with eWAT (C93-C97) uses co-clustering methods and shows partial overlap for some subpopulations but complete lack of overlap for lPRAT-ad3/ad4, supporting their uniqueness. The ASPC (C98-C101) and macrophage (C102-C108) comparisons similarly show substantial differences from eWAT. The age-related changes (C82-C84, C104) are well-quantified. The inference that differences suggest dissimilar microenvironments (C108) is reasonable and supported by citation (Lavin et al., 2014).

results.result: Re-clustering of ASPC populations reveals three subpopulations in both mPRAT and iBAT expressing Pdgfra. In mPRAT, aspc1 represents fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) expressing Dpp4/Pi16/Anxa3, while aspc2 and aspc3 are preadipocytes at different differentiation stages. Co-clustering shows high overlap between mPRAT and iBAT ASPCs with similar marker genes and good correspondence among subpopulations, suggesting they may give rise to similar adipocyte types. However, the PRAT-specific mPRAT-ad2 adipocyte subpopulation is absent in iBAT despite similar ASPCs, suggesting mPRAT-ad2 arises from brown-to-white conversion rather than ASPC differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C79 are supported by re-clustering analysis of ASPC populations (Figure 1—supplement 2A-K). The identification of three subpopulations in both depots (C70, C75) is based on gene expression patterns. The characterization of FAPs and preadipocytes (C71-C72) is consistent with known ASPC biology. The co-clustering analysis (C77) demonstrates high overlap between mPRAT and iBAT ASPCs. The inference that similar ASPCs may give rise to similar adipocytes (C78) is reasonable. The key inference (C79) that mPRAT-ad2 arises from conversion rather than ASPC differentiation is logical given the absence of mPRAT-ad2 in iBAT despite similar ASPCs, and is further supported by the lineage tracing experiments showing brown-to-white conversion.

results.result: snRNA-seq analysis of iBAT (27,717 nuclei) and iWAT (11,486 nuclei) under room temperature and cold exposure reveals depot-specific responses. In iBAT, cold exposure increases expression of brown adipocyte markers across all subpopulations including iBAT-ad4, and shifts proportions from iBAT-ad3 to iBAT-ad1, indicating cell-type conversions among Ucp1+ subpopulations. In iWAT, cold exposure induces beige adipocytes (iWAT-ad1, Ucp1+/Cidea+) and a lipogenic subpopulation (iWAT-ad2, expressing Acss2/Fasn/Acly) while reducing iWAT-ad4. ASPC proportions remain unchanged in both depots after cold exposure.
results.evaluation: Claims C160-C173 are supported by snRNA-seq analysis of iBAT and iWAT under both conditions (Figure 6—supplements 1-2). The lack of changes in overall cell type proportions (C160-C161) is shown in supplement figures. The transcriptomic similarity and increased BA marker expression (C162-C164) are demonstrated by gene expression analysis. The shift in iBAT subpopulation proportions (C165) and inference of cell-type conversions (C166) are supported by data and consistent with prior work (Song et al., 2020). The identification of cold-induced beige adipocytes in iWAT (C169) is expected. The identification of a lipogenic subpopulation (C170) is novel and supported by gene expression data, with agreement from recent literature (Holman et al., 2023). The unchanged ASPC proportions (C173) are consistent with findings in mPRAT.

results.result: Cell-cell communication analysis reveals that at room temperature, mPRAT adipocyte subpopulations show greater and stronger intercellular communication than iBAT or iWAT subpopulations, which may relate to ongoing brown-to-white conversion. Cold exposure reverses these relationships, reducing communication in mPRAT while increasing it in iBAT and iWAT. Thus, mPRAT adipocytes display very different levels of cell-cell communication compared to iBAT and iWAT under both conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C181-C184 are supported by CellChat analysis of ligand-receptor interactions (Figure 6F-G). The quantification shows clear differences in interaction numbers and strength between depots and conditions. The observation that mPRAT has higher communication at room temperature (C181) is well-documented. The speculation that this relates to brown-to-white conversion (C182) is reasonable but remains speculative as no direct mechanistic link is established. The reversal after cold exposure (C183) is clearly shown. The overall conclusion (C184) appropriately summarizes the findings. While the analysis is technically sound, the biological interpretation of what these communication differences mean functionally could be strengthened.

results.result: Background claims establish that PRAT is a unique visceral depot containing mixed brown and white adipocytes, with the medial region (mPRAT) containing UCP1-expressing brown adipocytes representing visceral BAT, while the lateral region (lPRAT) is predominantly white adipocytes. Prior studies suggest continuous replacement of brown by white adipocytes during aging in human PRAT, with potential for cold responsiveness. Brown-to-white conversion (whitening) is characterized by enlarged lipid droplets and reduced Ucp1 expression, and has been observed in various mammals but only in rabbit iBAT under normal physiological conditions.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C5-C31 are background/context claims supported by established knowledge and appropriate citations to prior literature. These claims accurately represent the current understanding of adipocyte biology (C5-C13), adipose tissue distribution (C16-C17), PRAT anatomy and composition (C18-C26), and the whitening phenomenon (C27-C31). The citations are appropriate and the characterizations are consistent with the cited literature. These claims provide necessary context for the study but do not represent novel findings.

results.result: Discussion claims contextualize findings within existing literature on brown-to-white conversion across species, explain transcriptomic differences based on developmental origins (mPRAT from Pax3+/Myf5- cells vs iWAT beige from multiple origins including Myh11+ precursors), discuss study limitations (single mouse strain, age range, lack of specific markers for mPRAT-ad2), and speculate on physiological significance and therapeutic potential. The authors note that mPRAT-ad2's intermediate phenotype (expressing both BA and WA markers) is consistent with its plastic nature, and that the majority of mPRAT-ad3/ad4 likely derive from ASPC differentiation rather than conversion.
results.evaluation: Claims C185-C229 represent discussion points that appropriately contextualize the findings within existing literature, provide reasonable interpretations of the data, acknowledge limitations, and suggest future directions. The citations to prior work on whitening in various species (C185-C189) and developmental origins (C215-C217) are appropriate. The interpretations regarding gene expression patterns (C194-C198, C203-C204) are reasonable inferences from the data. The speculation about physiological functions (C192, C225) and therapeutic potential (C228-C229) is appropriately framed as speculation. The acknowledged limitations (C220-C224) are valid. The inference that mPRAT-ad3/ad4 derive mainly from ASPCs (C199-C201) is supported by the lineage tracing data showing only small fractions express these markers.

results.result: The authors identify four adipocyte subpopulations in mPRAT through snRNA-seq, including a distinct Ucp1-&Cidea+ subpopulation (mPRAT-ad2) that is absent in iBAT. Trajectory analysis reveals a progressive brown-to-white transition during postnatal life, with decreasing proportions of mPRAT-ad1 and ad2 and increasing proportions of ad3 and ad4 from 1 to 6 months. Gene expression patterns along the pseudo-timeline show decreasing BA markers and increasing WA markers.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes 'there is overall a disconnection between single nucleus RNA-seq data and the lineage chasing data' and states 'No specific markers of this population have been validated by staining.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges the identification of the mPRAT-ad2 population but notes 'the limited sequencing depth of single nuclei somewhat lessens the impact of these findings.' The editor summarizes that evidence is 'convincing, although limited sequencing depth of single nuclei...somewhat lessens the impact.'

results.result: Using UCP1-lineage tracing (Ucp1CreERT2;Ai14 mice), the authors demonstrate that 61.8% of tdTomato+ cells in puPRAT lost UCP1 expression by 2 months, compared to only 7.5% in pvPRAT, indicating regional differences in brown-to-white conversion. Morphological analysis shows tdTomato+&UCP1- adipocytes display unilocular lipid droplets characteristic of white adipocytes. Immunostaining reveals that 34% and 23% of these whitened adipocytes express CYP2E1 and ALDH1A1, respectively, markers of mature white adipocyte subpopulations.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 requests validation of the lineage tracing system, stating 'The UCP1Cre-ERT2; Ai14 system should be validated by showing Tomato and UCP1 co-staining right after the Tamoxifen treatment.' This suggests concern about the specificity and efficiency of the lineage tracing approach. Reviewer 2 also notes the 'disconnection between single nucleus RNA-seq data and the lineage chasing data,' indicating that the integration of these two lines of evidence needs strengthening.

results.result: Cold exposure restores UCP1 expression and thermogenic phenotype in mPRAT, particularly in the mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation. The proportion of tdTomato+&UCP1- adipocytes decreased significantly after cold exposure in both puPRAT and pvPRAT. snRNA-seq analysis shows that mPRAT-ad2 cells completely disappeared after cold exposure while mPRAT-ad1 doubled, with no enhanced cell death observed. The authors conclude that new brown adipocytes induced by cold were mainly derived from UCP1- adipocytes rather than de novo ASPC differentiation in puPRAT.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 states 'It would be nice to provide more evidence to support the conclusion shown in lines 243 to 245 "These results indicated that new BAs induced by cold exposure were mainly derived from UCP1- adipocytes rather than de novo ASPC differentiation in puPRAT". Pdgfra-negative progenitor cells may also contribute to these new beige adipocytes.' This indicates the reviewers find the evidence insufficient to exclude alternative explanations for the origin of cold-recruited brown adipocytes.

results.result: The mPRAT-ad2 subpopulation has a transcriptome distinct from subcutaneous beige adipocytes (iWAT BeAs). At room temperature, little overlap exists between mPRAT and iWAT adipocyte subpopulations. Upon cold exposure, while iWAT BeAs show correspondence with a fraction of mPRAT-ad1, most mPRAT-ad1 adipocytes that arise from mPRAT-ad2 have a distinct transcriptome from cold-induced BeAs in iWAT. Even after cold exposure, thermogenic brown adipocytes in mPRAT are more similar to iBAT than iWAT.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly acknowledges this finding, stating 'The combination of UCP1-lineage tracing with the single nuclei analysis allowed the authors to identify four populations of adipocytes with differing thermogenic potential, including an "whitened" adipocyte (mPRAT-ad2) that retains the capacity to rapidly revert to a brown phenotype upon cold exposure.' The editor notes the work 'presents a valuable finding on the process of brown-to-white adipogenic transdifferentiation.' No reviewer challenges the transcriptomic distinctiveness of mPRAT-ad2 from iWAT beige adipocytes.

results.result: The authors profiled 11,708 nuclei from mPRAT and 31,079 nuclei from iBAT across three time points (1, 2, and 6 months). Six cell type clusters were identified in mPRAT and similar cell types in iBAT. Four adipocyte subpopulations were identified in both depots. Module score analysis revealed that mPRAT-ad1 was similar to iBAT brown adipocyte subpopulations (iBAT-ad1, 2, 3), while mPRAT-ad3 and ad4 were similar to iBAT-ad4.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes 'the limited sequencing depth of single nuclei somewhat lessens the impact of these findings,' which directly questions the robustness of the snRNA-seq data. The editor echoes this concern, stating the evidence is 'convincing, although limited sequencing depth of single nuclei...somewhat lessens the impact.' This suggests the reviewers accept the general findings but have reservations about the depth of the sequencing data.

results.result: ASPC populations in mPRAT, iBAT, lPRAT, and iWAT were characterized and subclustered into distinct subpopulations (FAPs and preadipocytes at different differentiation stages). Co-clustering revealed high similarity between mPRAT and iBAT ASPCs, suggesting they may give rise to similar adipocyte types. The proportions of ASPC subpopulations remained relatively unchanged after cold exposure in all depots examined.
results.evaluation: No reviewer raises concerns about the ASPC characterization or the finding that ASPC proportions remain unchanged after cold exposure. These findings are presented as supporting data for the main conclusions about adipocyte transdifferentiation rather than de novo adipogenesis being the primary mechanism of cold-induced browning.

results.result: The authors characterized lateral PRAT (lPRAT), identifying four adipocyte subpopulations and three macrophage subpopulations. Comparison with epididymal WAT (eWAT) revealed only partial overlap in adipocyte and ASPC populations, and very different macrophage populations. The cellular composition of lPRAT showed aging signatures, with decreased adipocyte proportion and increased macrophage proportion from 2 to 6 months.
results.evaluation: No reviewer challenges the lPRAT characterization. This depot serves as a control showing that not all perirenal adipose tissue undergoes brown-to-white conversion, and the reviewers do not question these findings. The characterization is treated as supporting context for understanding the unique properties of mPRAT.

results.result: UCP1 immunostaining revealed uneven distribution of UCP1-expressing brown adipocytes in mPRAT, with more intense staining in the perivascular region (pvPRAT) compared to the periureter region (puPRAT) in both juvenile and adult mice. UCP1 staining decreased in adult compared to juvenile mPRAT and was absent from lPRAT.
results.evaluation: No reviewer questions these anatomical observations. The regional heterogeneity within mPRAT is accepted as context for understanding the differential extent of brown-to-white conversion in different regions of the depot.

results.result: Using PdgfraCreERT2;Ai14 mice, the authors quantified the contribution of ASPC-derived adipocytes to cold-recruited brown adipocytes. In puPRAT, ASPC-derived BAs increased 2.3-fold while total cold-recruited BAs increased 10-fold. In pvPRAT, the increases were 4.4-fold and 2.2-fold, respectively. All adipocytes in both regions were 100% tdTomato+, indicating complete derivation from Pdgfra-expressing cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 specifically questions this conclusion, stating 'It would be nice to provide more evidence to support the conclusion...Pdgfra-negative progenitor cells may also contribute to these new beige adipocytes.' This directly challenges the interpretation that the difference between ASPC-derived and total cold-recruited adipocytes can be attributed solely to conversion from UCP1- adipocytes, suggesting alternative progenitor sources were not adequately ruled out.

results.result: snRNA-seq analysis of mPRAT, iBAT, and iWAT after cold exposure revealed depot-specific responses. In mPRAT, cold exposure dramatically altered adipocyte composition with mPRAT-ad2 disappearing and mPRAT-ad1 doubling. In iBAT, all adipocyte subpopulations increased BA marker expression and showed conversions among Ucp1+ subpopulations. In iWAT, cold-specific subpopulations emerged including BeAs (iWAT-ad1) and a lipogenic subpopulation (iWAT-ad2). Cell-cell communication analysis showed different patterns across depots under both room temperature and cold exposure conditions.
results.evaluation: No reviewer challenges these comparative findings across depots. Reviewer 3 notes 'the combination of well-executed lineage tracing with comprehensive cross-depot single-nuclei presented in this manuscript could still serve as a useful reference for the field,' indicating acceptance of the cross-depot comparisons despite concerns about sequencing depth.

comparisons.comparison: Both address lPRAT characterization (C80-C97, C102-C109). OpenEval finds the snRNA-seq analysis and comparisons with eWAT well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge, treating them as supporting context for understanding mPRAT's unique properties.

Both address lineage tracing of brown-to-white conversion in mPRAT (C114-C128). OpenEval finds the Ucp1Cre;Ai14 lineage tracing well-supported with quantitative data. Peer Reviewer 2 requests validation of the lineage tracing system and notes disconnection between snRNA-seq and lineage tracing data, indicating uncertainty about the approach.

Both address snRNA-seq data quality and adipocyte subpopulation identification (C32-C36, C47-C54). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with appropriate quality control. Peer Reviewer 3 and editor note that limited sequencing depth lessens impact, expressing uncertainty about robustness despite accepting general findings.

Both address mPRAT-ad2 identification and characterization (C37-C40, C42, C55-C56). OpenEval finds identification well-supported by clustering and gene expression. Peer Reviewer 2 notes lack of validated specific markers and disconnection between snRNA-seq and lineage tracing, while Reviewer 3 acknowledges identification but notes sequencing depth concerns.

Both address trajectory analysis and brown-to-white transition (C57-C65, C69). OpenEval finds longitudinal snRNA-seq and Monocle 3 trajectory analysis well-supported. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting disconnection between snRNA-seq and lineage tracing data and lack of validated markers for the mPRAT-ad2 population.

Both address ASPC characterization and similarity between mPRAT and iBAT (C70-C79). OpenEval finds the re-clustering analysis and inference that mPRAT-ad2 arises from conversion rather than ASPC differentiation well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these findings without raising concerns.

Both address transcriptomic distinctiveness of mPRAT-ad2 from iWAT beige adipocytes (C2-C4, C176-C179, C205-C206, C210). OpenEval finds comprehensive transcriptomic comparisons well-supported. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly acknowledges this valuable finding, and no reviewer challenges the transcriptomic distinctiveness, indicating support.

Both address cold-induced changes in iBAT and iWAT (C162-C172). OpenEval finds the snRNA-seq analysis of transcriptomic changes and subpopulation shifts well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these cross-depot comparative findings without challenge, with Reviewer 3 noting the combination of lineage tracing and single-nuclei analysis serves as useful reference.

Both address cold exposure experiments and recruitment mechanisms (C129-C136, C143-C144). OpenEval finds multiple complementary experiments well-supported with significant quantification. Peer Reviewer 2 requests more evidence to support conclusions about ASPC vs conversion origins, suggesting insufficient evidence to exclude alternative explanations.

Both address dual lineage tracing to distinguish ASPC-derived from conversion-derived adipocytes (C138-C142). OpenEval finds the use of both Ucp1CreERT2;Ai14 and PdgfraCreERT2;Ai14 mice well-supported. Peer Reviewer 2 questions this conclusion, suggesting Pdgfra-negative progenitor cells may contribute and that alternative sources were not adequately ruled out.

Both address acute cold exposure lineage tracing and compositional changes (C145, C151-C157). OpenEval finds the dramatic compositional changes and absence of enhanced cell death well-supported. Peer Reviewer 2 questions whether evidence sufficiently excludes alternative progenitor sources for cold-recruited adipocytes.

Both address regional differences in mPRAT (C110-C113). OpenEval finds anatomical observations of puPRAT vs pvPRAT differences well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these anatomical observations without question, treating them as context for understanding differential conversion extent.

Both address CellChat ligand-receptor interaction analysis (C181-C184). OpenEval finds the quantification of interaction differences well-documented but notes biological interpretation could be strengthened. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge as part of cross-depot comparisons.

Both address unchanged ASPC proportions after cold exposure (C158-C161, C173). OpenEval finds this supports limited de novo adipogenesis contribution. Peer reviewers accept these findings as supporting data for transdifferentiation being the primary mechanism rather than de novo adipogenesis.

Both address cold-induced changes across depots (C148-C150, C162-C172, C180-C184). OpenEval finds snRNA-seq analysis after acute cold exposure well-supported. Peer reviewers accept cross-depot comparative findings, with Reviewer 3 noting the comprehensive analysis serves as useful reference despite sequencing depth concerns.

OpenEval R11 addresses background/context claims (C1, C5-C31) about adipocyte biology, tissue distribution, and whitening phenomenon, finding them well-supported by established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are contextual rather than novel findings.

OpenEval R12 addresses discussion points (C185-C229) including contextualization, interpretations, limitations, and future directions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviews focus on primary data claims rather than discussion interpretations.
